captions.text: Breadth first search is layered exploration made rigorous.
A FIFO queue and a visited set that
together guarantees shortest paths in unweighted graphs at
optimal O(V+E) time. Remember the two things that bite people.
Mark nodes visited on enqueue, and watch the frontier memory
on wide graphs. Master BFS and you've mastered
the template that Dijkstra, A*, and every
shortest path system in production build upon.

scenes.title: Breadth-First Search
scenes.subtitle: The shortest-path algorithm
scenes.narration: Breadth-first search is the algorithm that answers a deceptively simple question: what is the fewest number of hops between two nodes in a graph? From the shortest chain of friends on a social network to the minimum moves in a puzzle, this 'distance by hop count' problem is everywhere. BFS solves it exactly, in linear time, using nothing more than a queue.

scenes.title: BFS: Level-Order Exploration
scenes.subtitle: Exploring the graph layer by layer
scenes.narration: The problem BFS solves is unweighted shortest path: find the minimum number of edges from a source to every other reachable node. Think of it as expanding a wavefront outward from the source, one ring of distance at a time.

data.title: The Key Insight
data.body: BFS visits all nodes at distance d before any node at distance d+1. The first time you reach a node is guaranteed to be the shortest path.

scenes.title: The FIFO Queue & Visited Set
scenes.subtitle: Two data structures powering BFS
scenes.narration: BFS depends on two data structures working together. The first is a FIFO queue: nodes are processed in the exact order they are discovered, which enforces the by-distance ordering. The second is a visited set that marks a node the moment it is first enqueued, not when it is dequeued. Marking on enqueue is the classic correctness detail.

operations.note: Add A's neighbor B to back
Add A's neighbor C to back
Remove C before D/E — preserves level order

data.title: Critical Rules
items: Mark visited on ENQUEUE, not dequeue
Use FIFO queue — not a stack
Visited set gives O(1) membership checks
A stack would turn BFS into DFS

scenes.title: The BFS Algorithm
scenes.subtitle: Every line matters
scenes.narration: The core loop is short but every line matters. Dequeue the front node, then scan its adjacency list. For each neighbor not yet in the visited set, mark it discovered, record its distance as current plus one, and enqueue it. Repeat until the queue empties.

data.title: BFS Implementation
⚠️ Common Mistake
data.body: If you mark visited on DEQUEUE instead of ENQUEUE, the same node gets pushed multiple times. This breaks the O(V) enqueue bound and corrupts shortest-path distances.

scenes.title: Why BFS Finds the Shortest Path
scenes.subtitle: The monotone-distance invariant
scenes.narration: Why is the first path found always the shortest? The proof rests on a monotone-distance invariant: at every point in the run, distances of nodes in the queue are nondecreasing and span at most two adjacent values, d and d+1. By induction, nodes leave the queue in nondecreasing distance order, so the first time a node is discovered it carries its true shortest distance.

steps.note: T reached at distance 3 — shortest path S→A→C→T

data.title: Time Complexity
data.description: BFS visits every vertex once and traverses every edge once — linear in the size of the graph. This is optimal.

scenes.title: BFS Complexity Analysis
scenes.subtitle: Time and space bounds
scenes.narration: BFS runs in O(V + E) time: every vertex is dequeued once and every edge is examined once. The catch is space. BFS is O(V) in memory, and the real killer is the frontier: at peak, the queue can hold an entire layer. In a branching graph with factor b and depth d, that frontier is O(b^d).

scenes.title: BFS vs DFS: The Trade-off
scenes.subtitle: Optimality vs memory
scenes.narration: BFS has three well-known failure modes and fixes. Memory blowup on wide graphs, mitigated by iterative deepening. Weighted edges that break the correctness proof, fixed by Dijkstra. And single-source search that explores too many nodes, fixed by bidirectional BFS.

data.title: BFS vs DFS Trade-offs
items: DFS: only O(depth) memory, no SP guarantee
Bidirectional BFS: O(b^(d/2)) instead of O(b^d)

data.title: BFS Cost Grows Linearly with Graph Size

scenes.title: BFS in Production
scenes.subtitle: Real-world applications
scenes.narration: BFS shows up in production far beyond textbooks. Web crawlers crawl in BFS order to reach high-value pages first. Network tools use BFS for shortest-hop routing. At scale, distributed graph engines like Pregel express BFS as vertex-centric supersteps, advancing one level per superstep across thousands of machines.

data.title: When to Use BFS vs Alternatives
pros: Simple to implement with a queue
O(V + E) time is optimal for this problem
GPS: min hops in road graphs
cons: O(V) space, frontier can be O(b^d)
Slow for deep targets in wide graphs

data.title: Real Systems
data.body: Google Pagerank crawling, LinkedIn 1st/2nd/3rd connections, network broadcast, maze solvers, Kubernetes dependency resolution.

scenes.title: BFS Architecture: Web Crawler
scenes.subtitle: BFS powering production crawl systems
scenes.narration: Web crawlers like Googlebot conceptually crawl in BFS order to reach high-value pages near seed URLs first. Distributed graph engines like Pregel and Apache Giraph express BFS as vertex-centric supersteps — each vertex processes its layer, sends messages to neighbors, and the frontier advances one BFS level per superstep.

data.title: LinkedIn Degrees
data.body: LinkedIn uses bidirectional BFS to compute 1st/2nd/3rd degree connections in real-time across 900M+ member graphs.

scenes.title: Master BFS
scenes.subtitle: The foundation of graph search
scenes.narration: The heart of BFS is one elegant idea: because a FIFO queue drains nodes in nondecreasing distance order, the first time you touch any node is guaranteed to be along a shortest path. Remember to mark on enqueue, watch the frontier for memory, and reach for Dijkstra or bidirectional BFS when the assumptions change.

data.title: Master BFS
data.subtitle: Mark on enqueue. FIFO queue. O(V+E) guaranteed.
